title: Combining Soreng with Pelling: routes and costs
meta_description: How to combine Pelling with Rinchenpong, Kaluk and Okhrey: drive times, the best order, 4 to 7 night plans, where to stay and indicative 2026 costs.
summary: Pelling and Soreng's Rinchenpong–Kaluk ridge are only about 35–40 km apart, 1.5–2 hours by road, which makes them easy to combine. Pelling gives you monasteries, Rabdentse and Khecheopalri Lake; Soreng gives you quiet villages and the Barsey rhododendron walk. Five nights split three and two is the sweet spot. Budget trips start around ₹15,000 per person.

sections.heading: Why pair Pelling with Soreng
paras: Pelling, at about 2,150 m in Gyalshing district (West Sikkim), is one of Sikkim's best-known hill towns. It sits close to some of the state's most important early history: Pemayangtse Monastery, Sanga Choeling, the ruins of Rabdentse, which served as the royal capital of Sikkim from the late 17th century until the early 19th, and Khecheopalri Lake, sacred to Buddhists and Hindus. It also has the widest choice of hotels in western Sikkim, from backpacker rooms to some of the best hotels in the state.

What Pelling does not have is quiet. In season the ridge fills with hotels and tour cars. Soreng, just to the south, is the opposite: farming villages, homestays, forest trails and the same Kangchenjunga view with a fraction of the traffic. Combining the two gives you the history and the comfort of Pelling with the calm of Rinchenpong, Kaluk or Okhrey, and the drive between them is short.
Most of our West Sikkim guests now do it this way, and it costs little more than staying in Pelling alone.

sections.heading: Drive times between the two
paras: Distances are short but the roads wind, so allow for the 20–25 km an hour average that is normal in the hills. Shared jeeps between Pelling and Soreng's villages are irregular, so for transfers a reserved car is much easier. All times below are typical in dry weather.

sections.heading: Which way round to go
paras: Both Pelling and Rinchenpong are 5–6 hours from NJP, so either can come first. We usually suggest Soreng first and Pelling second for two reasons. The quiet villages make a gentle landing after the long drive from the plains, and ending in Pelling, with its bigger hotels and restaurants, feels like a treat at the end of a trip. Pelling also has more cars for the return to NJP or onward to Gangtok.

Reverse it in April if the Barsey rhododendrons are your main reason for coming. Start in Pelling, then move to Okhrey for the walk once you have had a few days to get used to the hills, and finish with Rinchenpong or Kaluk on the way down to NJP.

In the monsoon both routes into the district from Siliguri use NH10 along the Teesta to Melli, which closes after landslides. The alternative is via Darjeeling to Jorethang, which adds one to two hours. Check current status before you travel.

If you are carrying on to Gangtok rather than returning to NJP, end in Pelling or go via Ravangla in Namchi district: Pelling to Gangtok is about 115 km and 5 hours, and the Ravangla route breaks the journey with Buddha Park and Ralang Monastery.

sections.heading: Four ways to put it together
paras: These are the shapes our guests choose most often. All start and end at NJP station or Bagdogra airport.

Our journeys pages show each of these as a priced package at budget, value and comfort level, with the price split line by line into stays, car, fees and planning, so you can see exactly what you are paying for and adjust it. Every itinerary can be shortened, lengthened or turned round to suit your dates.
list: 4 nights: Rinchenpong 2, Pelling 2. The shortest trip that does both justice
5 nights: Rinchenpong or Kaluk 2, Pelling 3. Adds a full day for Khecheopalri Lake and Yuksom
6 nights in April: Okhrey 2 for Barsey, Pelling 2, Yuksom 2
7 nights: Okhrey 2, Rinchenpong 2, Pelling 3. Barsey, the quiet ridge and Pelling's history in one loop

sections.heading: What to see on the Pelling side
paras: Give Pelling at least one full day. Pemayangtse Monastery, founded in the early 18th century and one of Sikkim's most important Nyingma monasteries, is a short drive or walk from town; the ruins of Rabdentse are a 20-minute forest walk from the road below it. Sanga Choeling, on a ridge above Pelling, is among the oldest monasteries in Sikkim and now sits near a large Chenrezig statue with a glass skywalk.

A second day can go to Khecheopalri Lake, about 1–1.5 hours away, where prayer flags line a quiet forest lake, and on to Yuksom, the village where Sikkim's first Chogyal was consecrated at Norbugang in the 17th century. Kanchenjunga Falls and the Singshore Bridge, near Dentam, can be seen on the way to Hilley or Uttarey.

On the Soreng side, a full day is enough for Rinchenpong Monastery, which Wikipedia dates to 1730 and which holds an unusual image of the Ati Buddha, the forest walk to Resum Gompa on the crest of the ridge, and a slow wander through orange and cardamom orchards to Kaluk. If you stay in Okhrey, the 4 km walk from Hilley to Barsey fills a morning, and the Sherpa village and its small monastery fill the afternoon. The pleasure on this side is less in sights than in time: sunrise from a terrace, dinner with your hosts, and roads with almost no traffic.

sections.heading: Where to stay on each side
paras: On the Soreng side, our stay guide to Rinchenpong and Kaluk covers homestays, Zostel Rinchenpong, Kaluk's village resorts and Yangsum Heritage Farm. In Okhrey, family homestays and small lodges are the only option and are part of the charm.

In Pelling, there is far more choice. Budget hotels on the main road charge about ₹1,500–3,000 a room. Comfortable mid-range hotels and resorts, such as Norbu Ghang Resort, cost roughly ₹5,000–10,000 a room. At the top end, The Elgin Mount Pandim, a heritage hotel below Pemayangtse, and The Chumbi Mountain Retreat are among the best hotels in western Sikkim, at about ₹12,000–25,000 a room. All prices are indicative 2026 bands; check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Practical tips for a combined trip
paras: Book the car for the whole trip rather than leg by leg. A driver who stays with you from NJP to NJP knows the plan, waits during walks and costs less overall than hiring at each stop. Make sure the car carries Sikkim tourist registration. In April and October to December, book Pelling hotels and Okhrey homestays four to six weeks ahead; Rinchenpong and Kaluk fill up later but are busy on long weekends.
list: Carry cash for the villages; Pelling has ATMs, Okhrey does not
Mobile signal is good in Pelling and on the Rinchenpong ridge, patchy around Okhrey and Hilley
Pack layers: Pelling and Okhrey nights are cold from November to March
Start drives early to avoid afternoon cloud and rain on the hill roads
Keep one spare day on trips of six nights or more

faqs.q: How far is Rinchenpong from Pelling?
faqs.a: About 35–40 km, which takes 1.5–2 hours on winding hill roads. It is an easy half-day transfer, leaving time to stop at viewpoints on the way. Shared jeeps between the two are irregular, so most travellers use a reserved car, roughly ₹2,500–3,500 for a small car. Check current status before you travel, especially in the monsoon.

faqs.q: Should I stay in Pelling or Rinchenpong?
faqs.a: If you have time, both. Pelling has the big sights, Pemayangtse, Rabdentse and Sanga Choeling, and the widest choice of hotels. Rinchenpong and Kaluk have quieter villages, homestays and the same Kangchenjunga view with far less traffic. Two nights in each, or two in Rinchenpong and three in Pelling, works well.

faqs.q: Can I visit Barsey on a day trip from Pelling?
faqs.a: Yes, but it is a long day. Hilley, the start of the 4 km Barsey walk, is about 75 km and 3–3.5 hours from Pelling via Dentam, so you face 6–7 hours of driving plus 3–4 hours walking. It is far more relaxed to spend two nights in Okhrey, about 10 km below Hilley, and walk to Barsey on the clearest morning.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Pelling and Soreng together?
faqs.a: Five nights is the sweet spot: two in Rinchenpong or Kaluk and three in Pelling, which allows a full day for Pelling's monasteries and Rabdentse and another for Khecheopalri Lake and Yuksom. Four nights works if you are short of time. In April, add Okhrey for the Barsey rhododendron walk and make it six or seven nights.

faqs.q: Which should come first, Pelling or Soreng?
faqs.a: We usually suggest Soreng first, for a quiet start after the long drive from NJP, and Pelling second, for its bigger hotels and easier onward connections to NJP or Gangtok. In April, if Barsey is the priority, start in Pelling, move to Okhrey for the walk and finish in Rinchenpong or Kaluk on your way back to NJP.

faqs.q: How much does a Pelling and Rinchenpong trip cost?
faqs.a: For five nights, two people sharing, from NJP and back, expect roughly ₹15,000–19,000 each on a budget, ₹24,000–30,000 at value level with a private small car, ₹35,000–45,000 at comfort level with an SUV and better hotels, and ₹75,000 or more at premium level. All figures are indicative for 2026.

faqs.q: Do I need permits for Pelling and Rinchenpong?
faqs.a: Indian travellers need no special permit for Pelling, Rinchenpong, Kaluk or Okhrey, only the ₹50 Sikkim tourist entry fee collected at check-in, and a forest fee for Barsey. Foreign nationals need Sikkim's Restricted Area Permit, applied for online on the e-FRRO portal after arrival in India. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I add Yuksom to a Pelling and Soreng trip?
faqs.a: Yes. Yuksom is about 35 km and 1.5–2 hours from Pelling, and two nights there let you see Norbugang, where Sikkim's first Chogyal was consecrated, Dubdi Monastery and Khecheopalri Lake on the way. A six- or seven-night trip of Soreng, Pelling and Yuksom is one of the best ways to see western Sikkim.

faqs.q: Is Pelling to Rinchenpong a good drive for children and seniors?
faqs.a: Yes. At 1.5–2 hours it is one of the shortest transfers in Sikkim, on a reasonable road with places to stop. Children prone to carsickness should sit in front and eat lightly before setting off. Both towns sit around 1,700–2,150 m, a moderate altitude that very few people have trouble with.
